{{Quote|Other worlds were spared: The Jakelians, for one, welcomed their new Mandalorian overlords ''[&hellip;]''<nowiki />|Vilnau Tept, 412th Proceedings of Galactic Anthropology and History|<ref name="EGTW" />}}
The '''Jakelians''' were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] from the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Jakelia system/Legends|Jakelia system]]. They developed edged [[Weapon/Legends|weapons]] and, during the [[Mandalorian Crusades]], became a vassal species of the [[Taung/Legends|Taung]] [[Mandalorian Crusaders]]. Later, during the [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|reign]] of [[Mandalore the Ultimate]], Jakelians were among the species whose members became full members of the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] clans.

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|And despite ''[the Mandalorian clans']'' nomadic ways, they were great tinkerers and canny technologists, improving Fenelar warships, Jakelian edged weapons, and even Republic rocket packs.|Vilnau Tept, 412th Proceedings of Galactic Anthropology and History|<ref name="EGTW" />}}
The Jakelians were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]]<ref name="EGTW" /> originating in<ref name="Planetnamia" /> the [[Jakelia system/Legends|Jakelia system]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Mandalore sector/Legends|Mandalore sector]].<ref name="EAOC" /> They developed edged [[Weapon/Legends|weaponry]]<ref name="EGTW" /> and shared their name with the [[Jakelian knife-dance]],<ref name="Cestus">''[[The Cestus Deception]]''</ref> a form of melee combat<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|135|Jakelian knife-dance}}</ref> that also possessed some characteristics of dancing.<ref name="Cestus" />

==Jakelians in the galaxy==
{{Quote|Mandalore the Ultimate's decision swelled the clans' ranks with humans, Mandallians, Jakelians, and other Mandalorian vassals.|Vilnau Tept, 412th Proceedings of Galactic Anthropology and History|<ref name="EGTW" />}}
[[File:MandaloreTheUltimateWithWickedGoldFlames-KOTOR15.jpg|thumb|right|300px|During the reign of Mandalore the Ultimate (pictured), Jakelians became full members of the Mandalorian clans.]]
At some point, the Jakelians came into contact with the [[Mandalorian Crusaders]], a culture of warriors originating with the [[Taung/Legends|Taung]] species and waging the [[Star/Legends|interstellar]] war-worship&ndash;based campaign known as the [[Mandalorian Crusades]] since [[7000 BBY]]. In contrast to other cultures that the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]] had [[Speciecide|exterminated]], the Jakelians readily accepted the conquerors as their new overlords and became their vassals. The Mandalorians, in turn, studied and improved the Jakelian edged weapons.<ref name="EGTW" />

At some point by [[3976 BBY]], the Mandalorian [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|leader]] [[Mandalore the Ultimate]] decreed that non-Taungs who proved themselves in battle and followed the [[Resol'nare|tenets]] of the Mandalorian warrior code would become full members of the Mandalorian clans, and consequently, Jakelians were among several species whose members thus became part of the warrior culture. [[Vilnau Teupt]] eventually mentioned the Jakelians in the keynote address "[[Industry, Honor, Savagery: Shaping the Mandalorian Soul]]" at [[Brentaal Academy]]'s [[Proceedings of Galactic Anthropology and History|412th Proceedings of Galactic Anthropology and History]] in [[24 ABY/Legends|24 ABY]].<ref name="EGTW" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Jakelians were mentioned in the [[2012]] reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Paul R. Urquhart]].<ref name="EGTW" />
